LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen hard from its highs and its profit margins are at a low point right now, but defense spending is steady and nothing about the long-term business has really broken — it's just a rough patch.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet this week — as the only company on earth making a certain kind of chipmaking machine, its price looks pretty normal for what it is, and there's no drama to report.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having an uneventful week supplying industrial gases under long contracts, and interestingly the market is pricing it unusually cheaply for a business this reliable.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm, with the big question being how fast its Azure cloud business keeps growing when it next reports — the AI story keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher had a nice week, and there's a good reason to be hopeful: money is flowing back into biotech companies, and that funding tends to turn into equipment orders for them a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge slipped a little, and its pipeline toll-road business keeps paying a solid dividend, though it isn't quite at the bargain level it sometimes reaches.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow jumped nicely this week — even though it's well off its high, it's outrunning its peers as big companies and government agencies keep adopting its AI workflow tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped a bit even as copper prices have been surging, which is a little odd — the mining-and-trading giant may be due to catch up to where the metal it digs out has already gone.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose after confirming the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still climbing nicely — the headline sales number looked soft only because of how the mix is reported, so the core business is as solid as ever.

KOF.sentence: This Latin American Coca-Cola bottler had a steady week, and the main thing that moves it for us is the Mexican peso's exchange rate, which is sitting in normal territory.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is enjoying high oil prices, which means fat profits and dividends right now — but those earnings are near a peak, so it may be a good moment to take a little off the table.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, drifted down this week and is now trading for less than its ships and assets are worth — a classic bargain-level for this kind of boom-and-bust business.

MA.sentence: No fresh data on Mastercard today, so there's nothing new to report on the payments network.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company had a quiet, slightly-up week, and the stock is actually cheaper than it's typically been over the past few years, even as hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines.
